source.title: Diagnosing Neural Convergence with Topological Alignment Spectra
source.authors: T. F. Tavares; F. Ayres; P. Smaragdis

record.file_problem: The full paper is present; some equations, figures and tables have flattened formatting.
record.tranche_reason: It measures representational alignment across scales with a different similarity method, and compares that method with other metrics.
record.gate_note: Table II reports pairwise similarity measurements for MultiBERTs models on SST2, IMDB and AG-News. The paper also reports synthetic point-cloud metric comparisons in Table I, but those results are not included here. It does not test model scaling or cross-modal alignment.
record.test_reason: The paper argues that the Platonic Representation Hypothesis's fixed k=10 mutual-neighbour test hides scale-dependent structure. It measures the same pair of different-seed MultiBERTs under many metrics and neighbourhood sizes, so its own results bear on metric dependence (V6), incomplete alignment (V7) and cross-seed convergence (V3). It has no scale, architecture or modality sweep.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that similarity is scale-dependent: different-seed models diverge locally but align at the semantic-cluster scale. Fine-tuning triggers comprehensive topological reorganisation that overrides pre-trained ancestry, which scalar metrics like CKA and GULP cannot resolve. They also argue that PRH's fixed k=10 is arbitrary and obscures misalignment at other scales.
record.recipe_differences: The paper presents a normalized mean-Jaccard neighborhood spectrum rather than the Platonic Representation Hypothesis's fixed k=10 comparison. It applies the spectrum to synthetic point clouds and MultiBERTs models.
record.method_sensitivity: Neighborhood size changes measured alignment; the reported metric also changes the apparent similarity. The paper reports results for three datasets and three model-comparison conditions.

fits_no_version.finding: On synthetic point clouds (Table I), CKA, Procrustes, GULP and RTD scores rise with dimensionality for the same distortion. TA stays constant, and local jitter vs shuffled cluster centres are conflated by scalar metrics.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Scalar representational similarity metrics are inflated by embedding dimensionality and conflate local and global distortions.

fits_no_version.finding: A pre-trained BERT and its own fine-tuned version show low TA across all k (0.03–0.25), while GULP stays 0.88–0.92.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fine-tuning reorganises representation topology at all scales even when predictive similarity stays high.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE International Joint Conference on Neural Network (as stated in the supplied metadata)
record.problems: The MultiBERTs case study uses two models from one collection with the same architecture and training task; no model scale or cross-modal comparison is made. Table II reports no uncertainty estimates. The paper's stated model evidence is limited to three datasets.
record.rows_left_out: Table II also reports CKA RBF, Procrustes, GW and PWCCA values for the same conditions; omitted to stay within the row limit while retaining TA, CKA Linear, GULP and RTD comparisons. Table I reports synthetic distortion comparisons across dimensions, omitted because the MultiBERTs results directly test the claim versions retained here.

untested.parts: No model-size or capability sweep; no comparison across architectures, objectives or data.
No vision-language or paired cross-modal comparison.
No unit-level, feature-level or subspace-matching analysis; only one seed pair, one architecture (BERT-base).
No mapping, stitching or relative-representation experiment. High GULP/GW is only interpreted by the authors as models being 'easily mapped'.
No interpretable features, neurons, SAE features or circuits.
Out-of-distribution inputs are not tested; only three in-domain text classification test sets.
Whether shared data or objectives, rather than a common model of reality, explain alignment is not tested; no plateau analysis with scale.

missing.what: Full TA spectra over k for each seed-pair comparison. FT-FT starts low, peaks near cluster size, then declines; this shape, not just two points, is the paper's main V6 evidence.
Procrustes, GW, PWCCA and CKA RBF values for PT-PT and FT-FT (e.g. SST2 PT-PT Procrustes 0.49, GW 0.99). Declared in rows_left_out but useful for V6 contrasts.

record.verdict_notes: I changed the tranche to T5 because the paper explicitly argues the PRH k=10 measurement needs restating, and its BERT results act as a test of that. PT-FT rows were unlinked: they compare a model with its own fine-tuned descendant, not independently trained models. V3 was added because PT-PT and FT-FT pairs differ only in seed, but the evidence is only one seed pair of one architecture, with no uncertainty reported. Shared data and objective are held fixed, so nothing here separates V7's causes. The 'high k' differs per dataset (910/1000/500, near cluster size), a selection made by the authors. Authors read high GULP/GW as models being easily mappable, but this is not a V4 mapping test.

versions.untested_parts: No model-size or capability sweep; no comparison across architectures, objectives or modalities.
No paired image-caption or other vision-language comparison.
It compares neighborhood geometry for same-architecture models initialized with different seeds, but does not test whether features or shared subspaces recur.
No mapping, stitching, relative-representation or unpaired interchangeability experiment is performed.
No interpretable features, neurons, SAE features or circuits are compared.
Metric and neighborhood-size sensitivity are tested on the stated datasets; out-of-distribution inputs and broader input-set variation are not tested.
The measurements show incomplete alignment across scales and model comparisons. The study does not test whether shared data or objectives, rather than a common model of reality, cause alignment.

relationships.condition: Different-seed MultiBERTs pairs (PT vs PT, FT vs FT) on SST2, IMDB, AG-News
relationships.reason: Same pair scores very differently by metric, e.g. SST2 PT-PT: GULP 0.99, CKA 0.64, TA(k=10) 0.12, RTD 0.06. TA also rises from k=10 to cluster-size k (0.12→0.74 SST2 FT-FT).
relationships.display_finding: A pretrained SST2 pair scored 0.99 under GULP, 0.64 under CKA, 0.12 under TA(k=10) and 0.06 under RTD; fine-tuned TA rose from 0.12 to 0.74 when k matched cluster size.
